newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador unions to decide strike date Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador unions to decide strike date Saturday.

text.p: Ecuadoran trade unions will fix a date Saturday for a national strike in protest at President Abdala Bucaram's tough economic reforms, the CMS labor federation said Friday.
Bucaram is facing his first protest rallies in five months in power against big hikes in public service tariffs.

Students held a third day of protests Friday against a hike of nearly 250 percent in domestic gas prices coming into effect next Monday. Police made 54 arrests and two students and seven police were injured in stone-throwing incidents.
The student protests were sparked by Wednesday's march of 5,000 people, led by teachers, through the center of Quito.

Oilworkers' leader Marcelo Roman, a CMS leader, told a news conference: "This national civic strike will be the start of a campaign to reject privatizations of strategic businesses and against rises in tariffs for basic services."
Bucaram hopes to sell off the state telephone and oil companies this year.

But the latest protests were sparked by Bucaram's plans, which he argues result from Congress watering down his tax reforms, to hike the price of a 15-kg gas cylinder to 10,000 sucres from 2,900 sucres. Speculation and hoarding has caused a shortage and cylinders are going for 30,000 sucres.

Opposition parties are forming a united front in Congress to fight Bucaram's attempts to raise utility tariffs and block the centerpiece of his reforms: currency convertibility involving egging the sucre to the U.S. dollar.
